# LittleWhale headless adaptations

Source: local `.tmp/LittleWhale`, commit `f21613fe86762f34d0f31c1a91c7a8aefd9acd19` (canonical DeepSeek Harness snapshot `b150a551b8d465e31e418e1b2eaf5e79bbb7d28e`). The source package manifests declare MIT, while LittleWhale's ownership manifest identifies the runtime packages as adapted upstream and its root assigns GPL-3.0-or-later to product-owned changes. Both the upstream [MIT notice](LICENSE) and the source project's [GPL notice](LITTLEWHALE-LICENSE) and [license reference](GPL-3.0-or-later.txt) are retained. These adaptations do not claim to relicense LittleWhale-owned changes. No UI, product composition, telemetry or coding tools are imported.

| Local component | LittleWhale source | Adaptation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `session.ts` | `packages/core/session/src/{index,surface}.ts`, `packages/core/agent-loop/src/{agent,tool-calls}.ts` | Headless port of append-only history, assistant/tool continuation and concurrent dispatch with ordered result publication. Replaces Cordis registries, scoped events, inboxes and chat turn management with explicit host capabilities and serializable pending calls. This is an adapted runtime, not an unmodified import of the concrete Cordis driver. |
| `tool-pairing.ts` | `packages/compaction/compaction/src/tool-pairing.ts` | Preserves balanced assistant/tool cuts. Emergent's `context-window.ts` lets history grow to 90% of the configured context window, then selects up to ten complete recent exchanges without old reasoning or checkpoints. |
| `json.ts`, `validation.ts` | `packages/core/session/src/json.ts`; pi-ai's TypeBox validation engine | Lossless JSON helper extracted unchanged. Standard JSON Schema bounds use pi-ai's underlying TypeBox engine directly without its argument-coercion wrapper. Emergent needs numeric, array and string bounds beyond LittleWhale's smaller raw-schema subset. |
| `server/inference/providers.ts` | `packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/{provider,discovery,replay,config}.ts` | Uses LittleWhale's pinned `@earendil-works/pi-ai@0.82.1` dependency for actual generation and native catalogs. Preserves catalog-provider dispatch, native response replay, endpoint-prefix model discovery and a streamed listing size bound. Replaces settings/credential services with a server-owned provider array; adds Emergent's Vast gateway transport and AWS discovery. |

The simulation owns time, physical concurrency, committed action IDs, perception and action validation. Tool promises carry world events; the session has no world reference. Foreground transport failures retain history and retry until cancellation. Completed tool results and pending calls are persisted before inference; `resumeTool` rebinds pending call IDs to existing action receipts.

Conversation summarization is removed. Each acting request keeps its stable conversation prefix and appends a fresh entity-scoped observation and current memory record. Provider-reported prompt usage calibrates the pressure estimate; only at 90% of the configured context window does the session retain a bounded recent raw tail. Response limits do not affect conversation pressure. Original messages and reasoning remain in durable events and inference audits, and each compaction is recorded in the world journal. Existing snapshots migrate on their next request without resetting goals, receipts or world state.

Emergent's `server/agents/memory-record.ts` independently compresses intent, private notes and learned knowledge using the complete current acting context. Its 3943-byte UTF-8 JSON threshold is the larger record measured at First Shore tick 2028 (Moss 3888, Flint 3943). Each write cancels obsolete work and starts a new attempt if still above threshold. Only validated, strictly smaller output for the same revision is published. Failure, truncation or non-reduction keeps the original and waits for a new write, including after restart. Compaction output does not trigger itself.

Background memory inference uses a separate 8192-token request budget and bypasses the foreground serial queue. It never participates in the world-time barrier. Shared provider hardware can still affect inference latency. Compacted records and outcomes are recorded for observer replay; original discoveries remain available through `recall`. Token metrics include background requests and preserve reasoning-only truncation usage.
